newsitem.title: UK: Copper, other metals rally after brief correction.
newsitem.headline: Copper, other metals rally after brief correction.

text.p: Copper and other base metals regained a firmer tone on Wednesday after a shortlived downside correction this week.
Analysts said that although the flagship copper market was overheated and had needed a technical breather, it still seemed to be locked firmly in a short term uptrend.
"Having had a long run up -- from $2,140 at the end of January to a high of $2385 -- it was in need of a technical correction," said analyst William Adams of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
"But the upward trend, having broken above $2,315 last week, pushes it towards $2,450," he said, referring to the technical picture for three months copper prices.
On Wednesday afternoon copper prices rallied on speculative buying to a high of $2,382 per tonne, close to the June 1996 high of $2,385 achieved on Monday.
It had started the day much weaker at $2,335, after profit-taking on Tuesday had undercut recent gains.
The decline on Tuesday in copper was probably sparked in part by smaller than expected LME stock declines, Adams said.
But with the cash/threes backwardation narrower around $70, compared to above $300 several weeks ago, consumer buying interest was boosted which was helping keep prices underpinned, he added.
Aluminium and nickel, which like copper had crumbled after hitting nine-month highs on Tuesday, also managed to snap back.
Aluminium prices approached the recent high of $1,663 in afternoon LME ring trading on Wednesday, strongly up from the morning's low of $1,639.
Nickel also rallied nearly $200 from the day's lows to regain the $8,000 level following news that workers at Russia's Norilsk Nickel plant were considering going on strike on March 15.
But although concerns over Norilsk have helped boost prices, the threat of a strike will likely have limited bullish impact on the market, analysts said.

"Norilsk is a perennial problem. Even if there is a strike on March 15 it is unlikely to disrupt output and exports that much, unless it is very prolonged," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.
Despite the correction, short term uptrends in copper, aluminum and nickel remained solidly in place, he added.
"But the next three months will be crucial as demand in the metals market picks up and peaks," Bhar said.
The expectation that China will be a big buyer of copper and other base metals is also key to the price direction of many of the base metals, especially copper, analysts said.
